Andrew Carnegie, once the richest man alive, hired a researcher named Napoleon Hill to study the truly wealthy — Henry Ford, Thomas Edison, J.P. Morgan — and write down exactly what they knew that nobody else did.

Hill published it in 1926. Henry Ford saw the finished book and killed it — "we don't want people to know the truth" — and had it pulled from the market. What came back years later was a watered-down version. What came back after that, even more watered down, was Think and Grow Rich. Millions have read it. Almost none got the actual secret.
